description:
Advances: specled.package

Review-bar-override: a gate proposal, not a defect — the class recurs across reviews and should stop being reportable.

From the critical review of specled_-n5q (Recurring class 2).

docs_identifier_lint_test is one-directional today: it rejects doc references to finding codes that do not exist in lib, but it does not verify that docs ENUMERATE every code that does. So a table claiming to list "the full set of branch-guard codes" silently goes stale the moment a code is added, and the claim becomes false with nothing failing.

This has now bitten repeatedly: docs/adoption.md full-set claim (fixed on this branch), the finding_code_budget "tenth code" total with no counting rule (fixed on this branch), and the spec-prose overclaim class generally, which is a standing review checklist item.

Making the lint bidirectional mechanizes the enumeration half permanently. The phrase-level overclaims (comparatives with no basis, "impossible" where the truth is "deferred") stay a review concern — those are not mechanizable.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.package

Specifically specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity (.spec/specs/package.spec.md:112-115),
which is priority: must, stability: STABLE. Amending a STABLE must is the higher bar here — the
amendment is strictly STRENGTHENING (it adds an obligation), so append_only will not flag it and
no weakening ADR is needed, but route the exact must wording past a human in your completion
record. That requirement is already ~900 words of load-bearing prose, and growing it is
precisely the class specled_-vzd.3 exists to catch.

Allowed touches:
- test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs
- .spec/specs/package.spec.md
- docs/adoption.md  (full-set-claim markers)
- docs/concepts.md  (ONLY if it carries a real full-set claim — see below, it does not)
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md  (amendment, only if the
  lint's corpus scope changes)

Out of Scope (files):
- all of lib/**
- skills/**, README.md
- any other .spec/decisions/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT implement "every known code must appear somewhere in docs." Measured at the epic base:
  docs + skills + README currently name 3 of 11 append_only/*, 2 of 2 overlap/*, 0 of 7
  evidence/*, and 0 of 8 cross_field/*. A whole-corpus reverse lint fails on 21 codes on day
  one. The lint MUST be scoped to explicitly-marked full-set-claim regions.
- Do not attempt phrase-level overclaims (comparatives with no basis, "impossible" where the
  truth is "deferred"). The ticket rules them out as non-mechanizable.
- Do NOT replace the hand-maintained @known_codes with reflection.
  specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus forbids it, and
  docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:59-62 restates why.

CONCRETE DESIGN TO LAND: region markers, e.g.
  <!-- spec-lint:full-set=branch_guard_gated --> ... <!-- spec-lint:full-set-end -->
plus a per-marker expected-set map in the test. The two live claim sites are
docs/adoption.md:43 ("The full set of branch-guard codes mix spec.check gates on:", table at
:47-56, 8 codes) and docs/adoption.md:58-68 (triangulation-only table, 3 codes). 8 + 3 = 11 =
@branch_guard_codes (docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:127-139), so the family partitions cleanly
across two marked regions and the lint asserts the union equals the family.
docs/concepts.md:189 ("The full set is in the ...") is a POINTER, not a claim — it must NOT be
marked. Mirror the existing marker discipline; the family-count speed-bump test at
docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:322-335 is the precedent.

Verification:
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs
  mix test --only spec:specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity
  mix format --check-formatted
  make xref
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
NO stub flip: package.spec.md:126-132 already covers doc_identifier_integrity at execute: true.
New tests carry @tag spec: "specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity", or a new sibling id added
to that same covers: list.

Expected diff: 3-4 files, ~160 lines.

Summary: Added explicit full-set markers around the two adoption-guide claim regions and a bidirectional lint that rejects malformed, missing, duplicated, incomplete, overlapping, or overbroad configured claims. Stable-must wording for human review: “Every documentation region explicitly marked as a full-set claim shall enumerate exactly its configured expected set, and the configured branch-guard claim sets shall partition the full hand-maintained branch-guard family so adding or removing a code makes an incomplete or overbroad claim fail the lint.” The lint retains the existing corpus and hand-maintained implementation-code mirror, and the concepts pointer remains unmarked.

VERIFY: PASS
Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f.jsonl

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 3 (test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs, docs/adoption.md, .spec/specs/package.spec.md)
- Files outside Allowed globs: 0
- Files matching Out-of-Scope globs: 0 (no lib/**, no skills/**, no README.md, no .spec/decisions/**)
- Worktree clean after verification (git status --porcelain empty); all mutations run on a scratch rsync copy outside the repo, deleted afterwards.

Does the lint bite (mutation results, scratch copy, baseline there = 21 tests / 0 failures):
- (a) delete the `branch_guard_dangling_binding` row from the marked gated table (docs/adoption.md:50): RED
    "docs/adoption.md:45: full-set claim \"branch_guard_gated\" is missing [\"branch_guard_dangling_binding\"]"
- (b) inject a real-but-wrong code row (`branch_guard_untested_realization`) inside the gated region: RED
    "docs/adoption.md:45: full-set claim \"branch_guard_gated\" has unexpected [\"branch_guard_untested_realization\"]"
- (c) add a genuinely new code to lib (branch_check.ex @per_code_defaults) AND to @branch_guard_gated_codes, but NOT to docs: RED  <-- the ticket's whole point
    "docs/adoption.md:45: full-set claim \"branch_guard_gated\" is missing [\"branch_guard_brand_new_code\"]"
    Note: the pre-existing mirror-drift test stayed GREEN under (c) (the mirror matched lib correctly). The ONLY failing test was the new full-set claim test — i.e. this is exactly the regression that was previously invisible.

Two extra mutations beyond the contract, to rule out escape hatches:
- (d) delete both marker pairs from docs/adoption.md entirely: RED
    "full-set claim \"branch_guard_gated\" must occur exactly once, found 0" (+ same for triangulation).
    Removing the markers is not a way to go green.
- (e) add a third hand-maintained family list to @branch_guard_codes without a @full_set_claims entry: RED
    "configured branch-guard full-set claims no longer partition @branch_guard_codes"
    Proves the partition assertion (test:383) is non-vacuous, not just a tautology over the derived attribute.

Scoping and discipline:
- Lint scoped to marked regions, not whole-corpus: by design. full_set_regions/1 streams the corpus and only accumulates lines BETWEEN a `<!-- spec-lint:full-set=<id> -->` / `<!-- spec-lint:full-set-end -->` pair (test:611-658); full_set_region_violations/1 compares only those lines against @full_set_claims (test:660-679). There is no assertion anywhere that a known code must appear in docs. Verified empirically: the ~21 codes with zero doc mentions (0/7 evidence/*, 0/8 cross_field/*, 8/11 append_only/*) do not fail anything — the suite is green at HEAD.
- The two marked regions partition @branch_guard_codes exactly (8 + 3 = 11): asserted at test:383 (union == family) and test:386 (union size == sum of sizes, i.e. no overlap). @branch_guard_codes is now DERIVED as @branch_guard_gated_codes ++ @branch_guard_triangulation_codes (test:144), and @full_set_claims is built from those same two lists (test:146-149) — so a code cannot enter the family without entering exactly one claim set. Non-vacuousness proved by mutation (e).
- Region structure is also guarded: nested start marker, end-without-start, unterminated region, unknown claim id, and claim-id occurrence count != 1 all produce violations (test:357-369, 627-657).
- docs/concepts.md:189 pointer NOT marked: confirmed. `grep -rn "spec-lint:full-set"` across the repo returns exactly 4 hits, all in docs/adoption.md (45, 60, 68, 76). concepts.md:189 ("The full set is in the ...") carries no marker.
- Hand-maintained mirror preserved, no reflection introduced: @known_codes is still MapSet.new(@append_only_codes ++ @overlap_codes ++ @evidence_codes ++ @cross_field_codes ++ @branch_guard_codes) (test:151-155), all hand-written ~w() literals. The diff adds no reflection; implementation_guarded_codes/0 (the pre-existing mirror-drift anchor, which reads lib source text, not runtime reflection) is untouched. The moduledoc rationale at test:59-62 is unchanged.
- One incidental fix worth noting as correct: guarded_tokens/1 now strips the full-set START marker line (test:747), because the marker id `branch_guard_gated` itself matches the `branch_guard_[a-z_]+` token pattern and would otherwise be reported as a fabricated code. The strip is anchored (^...$) so it can only remove a whole marker line, never real prose.
- The `append_only/*` and `overlap/*` rows inside the gated table do not pollute the actual set: `[a-z_]+` cannot match `*`, so they yield no tokens.

Stable-must amendment:
- New must wording (one sentence inserted after the mirror-drift sentence): "Every documentation region explicitly marked as a full-set claim shall enumerate exactly its configured expected set, and the configured branch-guard claim sets shall partition the full hand-maintained branch-guard family so adding or removing a code makes an incomplete or overbroad claim fail the lint."
- Accurate about what the lint actually enforces: YES. Clause by clause:
    * "explicitly marked as a full-set claim" — correctly scopes to marker-delimited regions. It does NOT claim prose full-set claims generally are enforced, which is the overclaim that would have been self-refuting here.
    * "shall enumerate exactly its configured expected set" — matched by the bidirectional missing/unexpected comparison, mutations (a) and (b).
    * "the configured branch-guard claim sets shall partition the full hand-maintained branch-guard family" — matched by test:383 and test:386, proved live by (e). "hand-maintained" is the honest word: it is not derived from lib.
    * "so adding or removing a code makes an incomplete or overbroad claim fail the lint" — matched by (a)/(c) for removal-from-docs / addition-to-family, and (b) for overbroad.
  No exhaustive definite description, no comparative without basis, no total without a counting rule, and nothing labelled impossible that is merely deferred.
- append_only findings against this diff: NONE. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` -> `validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0`, `branch base=origin/main changed_files=3 findings=0 (error=0 warning=0 info=0)`, `spec.check result=pass`. The amendment is purely additive prose on a STABLE must, so append_only correctly treats it as strengthening.

Semantic checks:
- Spec stubs run: 0 flipped (contract said none required; package.spec.md:126-132 already covers doc_identifier_integrity at execute: true). Both new tests carry @tag spec: "specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity".
- Targeted verification (all in /Users/mz/src/specled_ex-bidirectional-doc-lint):
    mix compile --warnings-as-errors -> clean
    mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs -> 21 tests, 0 failures
    mix test --only spec:specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity -> 3 properties, 1325 tests, 0 failures, 1307 excluded
    mix format --check-formatted -> pass
    make xref -> pass (compile-connected --fail-above 0)
    mix spec.check --no-run-commands -> spec.check result=pass
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only, no action required):
- Nothing forces a NEW prose full-set claim to carry a marker — a future author can still write "the full set is X, Y, Z" unmarked and it stays unlinted. That is inherent to the marked-region design the contract mandated, and the ticket explicitly rules phrase-level detection out of scope. Worth remembering when a third claim site is added.
- The marker id grammar is `[a-z0-9_]+`. Any id that happens to start with a guarded prefix (as both current ids do, via `branch_guard_`) relies on the guarded_tokens/1 strip. That is handled, but an id like `evidence_foo` would be fine while `evidence/foo` would not be a legal id anyway — no issue today, just a coupling to keep in mind.
- @full_set_claims currently only covers branch_guard. If append_only/* or evidence/* ever get a marked full-set table, the partition assertions at test:383-387 will need a per-family generalization rather than the single hardcoded @branch_guard_codes comparison.

TEST_CRITIC: PASS
Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f.jsonl

Graded: HEAD 686fca31 on base bb64e69e (epic specled_-i4x).
All mutants built on scratch copies outside the repo; worktree left clean.

- Mutant (a) row deleted: RED. Deleted the `branch_guard_dangling_binding` row from the marked gated table -> `docs/adoption.md:45: full-set claim "branch_guard_gated" is missing ["branch_guard_dangling_binding"]`. New test only.
- Mutant (b) bogus row added: RED, twice. Inserted `branch_guard_completely_invented` inside the marked region -> new test reports `has unexpected [...]` AND the pre-existing fabricated-code test fires. Also ran the sharper variant the pre-existing lint CANNOT catch — a REAL code in the wrong table (`branch_guard_untested_realization` moved into the gated region): RED on the new test alone. That is the added value, confirmed.
- Mutant (c) real code added to family, docs not updated: RED, and confirmed newly closed by control. Added `branch_guard_brand_new_gate` to `lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex` @per_code_defaults AND to `@branch_guard_gated_codes` (so mirror-drift stays green), docs untouched -> `full-set claim "branch_guard_gated" is missing ["branch_guard_brand_new_gate"]`. Same mutation replayed against base bb64e69e: 19 tests, 0 failures — GREEN. The ticket's target regression is genuinely closed.

- Self-fulfilling check: NO. Two independent sources. Expected set comes from the test's hand-maintained `@branch_guard_gated_codes` / `@branch_guard_triangulation_codes` (test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:127-149), which are anchored to lib/ by the pre-existing mirror-drift test via `implementation_guarded_codes/0` scanning `@implementation_code_files`. Actual set is parsed out of `docs/adoption.md`. Neither side reads the other. Mutant (c)'s control run is the proof: change lib+family only and the docs side does not follow.

- Failure-message content asserted: YES. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:405-410 pins the exact diagnostic strings, naming both the omitted code (`branch_guard_underspecified_realization`) and the unexpected one (`branch_guard_realization_drift`), with file:line prefix. Not a bare "it raised".

- Marker parsing robustness: LOUD in every malformed case probed by execution — unterminated region ("full-set claim has no end marker"), orphan end marker ("end marker has no start marker"), nested markers ("nested full-set claim marker" + unknown-claim), duplicate region for a known id ("must occur exactly once, found 2"), both markers deleted ("found 0" for both claims), marked region with no table (missing all 8/3 codes). Trailing whitespace after the marker is tolerated (correct). Typo'ing the start marker (`full-set = ` with spaces) fails TWICE: the count check plus the fabricated-code lint, because the unmatched marker id is itself `branch_guard_*`-shaped and no longer stripped by `guarded_tokens/1`. No silent-pass evasion path found: the exactly-once count check on `@full_set_claims` keys is the backstop that a typo cannot get around.

- Sweep: no Process.sleep, `async: true`, no shared/global state introduced, no `@tag` drift, both new tests carry `spec: "specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity"`. Findings, none blocking:
  1. `full_set_regions_for_file/1` (the marker parser, lines 618-658) has ZERO controlled-input tests. Test 1 only runs it over a well-formed corpus, so every violation branch is dead in a passing run; test 2 bypasses the parser entirely by handing a synthetic region to `full_set_region_violations/1`. I proved those branches work by mutation, but nothing in the suite defends them — delete the nested-marker branch and the suite stays green. This is below the file's own established bar: the allow-marker grammar next door has 8 controlled-input tests including a dedicated `>`-in-reason-text regression (line 571).
  2. The gated-vs-triangulation bucket split is unanchored to the implementation. `@known_codes` is mirror-checked against lib/, but WHICH bucket a branch_guard code lands in is pure hand-maintenance. Moving a genuinely-gated code into `@branch_guard_triangulation_codes` and into the triangulation table is fully green, so the docs can misclassify a gate as diagnostic-only and the lint approves.
  3. Line 383's partition assertion (`claimed_branch_guard_codes == MapSet.new(@branch_guard_codes)`) is tautological — it cannot fail while `@full_set_claims` is built from the same two attributes `@branch_guard_codes` concatenates. The disjointness assertion at line 386 IS real (verified: duplicating a code across buckets fires).
  4. Sharp edge: the region's actual set is extracted with `guarded_tokens/1`, which matches all five families, while the expected set is branch_guard-only. The `append_only/*` and `overlap/*` rows inside the marked gated region pass only because `*` does not match `[a-z_]+`. Expanding either wildcard to a real code — making the docs strictly MORE accurate — turns the lint RED (`has unexpected ["append_only/requirement_deleted"]`, verified). Future editors will hit this.
  5. Minor: test 2 is a pure unit test over a test-local private helper and can never fail for a docs reason; test 1 is the only one that pins the document. Fine as a pair, worth knowing.

Verdict rationale: The load-bearing question resolves cleanly — all three mutants turn the suite RED, and mutant (c), the regression the ticket exists to prevent, is demonstrably GREEN on base and RED after, so the new check is what closes it. The comparison is genuinely bidirectional and not self-fulfilling: expected comes from the lib-anchored code mirror, actual from the document, and the control run separates them. Malformed markers fail loudly with named diagnostics rather than silently disabling the check. The one real gap is that the new marker parser is itself undefended by controlled-input tests, but that is a hole in protecting the new machinery, not one that reinstates the defect the ticket closes — so it is a follow-up, not a FAIL.

title: Make docs_identifier_lint bidirectional so full-set claims cannot go stale
